title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-lena-martin
content:
Scratchpad - model loading failure breadcrumbs

TL;DR: intermittent failures when loading the 30B model after switching to shard-bytes packaging (safetensors). Errors observed include checksum/hash mismatches, unexpected tensor shapes, and mmap-related failures on NFS mounts. Repro steps, commands tried, and hypotheses below.

Environment:
- runtime branch: main (commit: 7f3c2d)
- serving binary: redwood-runtime v1.12.0-dev
- host: g4dn.xlarge (Ubuntu 22.04), NFS-mounted /models volume
- python: 3.11.4, torch 2.2.0, safetensors 0.3.0, bitsandbytes 0.39.0
- model packaging change: moved from single .pt -> sharded safetensors (shard_000.safetensors .. shard_011.safetensors)

Observed failures (examples):
1) Checksum/partial download suspicion
- error log snippet:
  [2025-11-03 09:12:47,215] ERROR load: Failed to load shard shard_007.safetensors: checksum mismatch (expected 7b2a1f3c..., got 5c9d2a1e...)
- symptoms: model load aborts during state_dict merge, restart helps sometimes

2) Tensor shape mismatch while strict-loading
- error:
  RuntimeError: size mismatch for transformer.layers.10.self_attn.k_proj.weight: copying a param with shape torch.Size([2048, 4096]) from checkpoint, the shape in current model is torch.Size([1024, 4096]).
- occurs after loading checkpoint produced by new compilation pipeline (converted/resized)

3) mmap / OOM when mapping large shard files on NFS
- error:
  OSError: [Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory when doing mmap on /models/model-x/shard_000.safetensors
- observed during warmup on nodes with low available mem but plenty of disk

Reproduction checklist (quick):
- refresh model cache: rm -rf /models/model-x && mkdir -p /models/model-x && export MODEL_DIR=/models/model-x
- gsutil cp gs://redwood-models-x/30b-sharded/* $MODEL_DIR/
- sha256sum *.safetensors > checksums.txt
- run: python -m redwood_runtime.load_model --model-dir $MODEL_DIR --device cpu --no-mmap

Commands tried (with notes):
- Download attempts:
  - gsutil -m cp -r gs://redwood-models-x/30b-sharded/* /models/model-x/  # initial
  - gsutil -m rsync -r gs://redwood-models-x/30b-sharded /models/model-x  # tried to recover file perms/partial
  - curl -C - -L https://cdn.redwood.ai/models/30b/shard_007.safetensors -o shard_007.safetensors /* manually resume */
  - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/30b-sharded/shard_007.safetensors . --no-progress
  Note: observed different file sizes between endpoints (cdn vs gs).

- Checksum/verify:
  - sha256sum *.safetensors | sort > local_sums.txt; diff local_sums.txt expected_sums.txt  # mismatch on shard_007, shard_009
  - python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; print(safe_open('shard_007.safetensors').metadata)"  # shows truncated metadata on bad file

- Load attempts:
  - python -c "import torch; s=torch.load('shard_007.pt', map_location='cpu')"  # not used (we shifted to safetensors)
  - python -c "from safetensors.torch import load_file; d=load_file('shard_007.safetensors'); print(len(d))"  # raises EOFError on bad shard
  - redwood-runtime --model-dir /models/model-x --load-mode eager --map-location cpu  # failed at shard 7
  - redwood-runtime --model-dir /models/model-x --no-mmap --load-mode lazy  # avoided OOM but then hit shape mismatch later

- Conversion/repair attempts:
  - ran convert_checkpoint.py from tooling/ to regenerate safetensors from canonical .pt (local) -> produced identical checksums for shards on my laptop (so conversion likely fine)
  - tried re-uploading shard_007 after re-conversion -> new checksum; cluster still sometimes receives old file (possible CDN cache)

Hypotheses and notes:
- H1: Broken upload / partial CDN replication. Evidence: different sizes across endpoints and intermittent success after reupload. Action: add artifact versioning + immutable filenames (not overwrite).
- H2: Clients loading with mmap on NFS hitting kernel limits -> partial read leading to EOF/ checksum errors. Evidence: OSError mmap observed; switching to --no-mmap avoids mmap error. Action: use copy-to-local-temp before loading on NFS or change fs mount options.
- H3: Incompatible serialization/ordering expectations across safetensors versions or conversion tool. Evidence: EOFError and truncated metadata on some shards. Action: pin safetensors lib and add CI check that safe_open can open all shards on upload.
- H4: Model config mismatch (architecture/hidden size) vs checkpoint. Evidence: size mismatch for attention proj weights. Could be wrong model variant used for serving. Action: verify model.json / config.json included in model bundle and assert on load.

Immediate mitigations tried and outcomes:
- Force re-download to local disk on each node before load (copy to /tmp) -> reduced mmap/OOM errors but did not fully eliminate shape mismatch failures.
- Pin safetensors 0.3.0 on runtime nodes -> no immediate change for the corrupted shards; but consistency across nodes improved.
- Add pre-load verification script that attempts to safe_open each shard and fail fast with clear message (added to startup script).

Next steps (TODOs):
- [ ] Add immutable naming and version manifests for model bundles (no in-place overwrite) - infra task (INF-2134).
- [ ] Audit CDN/GS replication delays and add strong checksum verification at edge (SRE)
- [ ] Add load-time assertion that model config matches checkpoint (size, num_layers, vocab) and fail with actionable error
- [ ] Add copy-to-local (tmpfs) step for NFS-backed hosts or prefer local disk cache
- [ ] Add CI job to open all safetensors shards with current safetensors version before release
- [ ] Investigate improving runtime to fallback from strict->partial load (strict=False) with schema validation and migration warnings

Notes for handoff to SRE/Infra:
- Provide list of affected shards and hashes (attached to ticket). Suspect CDN caching or gsutil partial-transfer behavior when upload was interrupted.
- Recommend pushing artifact gating to release pipeline: only publish after successful remote open (safetensors safe_open) and sha256 verification.

Breadcrumbs (quick timeline):
- 2025-11-02: rolled new sharded packaging pipeline -> small % of infra nodes saw failures
- 2025-11-03: observed repeated shard_007 checksum mismatch; attempted reupload (PR #482)
- 2025-11-04: pinned safetensors and added pre-load verification script to runtime startup
- 2025-11-05: still seeing occasional shape mismatch on canary nodes -> likely config mismatch between model bundle and runtime model variant

Logs / stuff to attach to ticket:
- sha256 manifest (local)
- gsutil ls -l output for model dir across regions
- sample runtime logs (error snippets above)
- convert_checkpoint.py output and local checksums

If I (Lena) don't get to this in next 24h: handoff to Ethan + SRE; leave pre-load verify script in place and block rollout until all shards pass safe_open and checksum.

End of scratchpad.
